summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) is the Korean government's degree scholarship for international students, run by NIIED under the Ministry of Education. The undergraduate track gives one year of Korean-language training and then an associate degree (2 to 3 years) or a bachelor's degree (4 to 6 years). The graduate track gives one year of Korean-language training and then a master's (2 years) or a doctorate (3 years). Applicants and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship. Selection is by the Korean embassy or the university, then NIIED, and for the embassy track a final round at the universities.
eligibility_notes:
Citizenship: the applicant must be a citizen of a country NIIED has invited, and the applicant's parents or legal guardians must hold citizenship other than Korean. A person with dual Korean citizenship, or a parent with dual Korean citizenship, is not eligible. Anyone who held Korean citizenship before (applicant or parent) must show documents from the Korean government proving the renunciation. If the applicant's citizenship changes during selection, the application is dropped. The university-industry cooperation (UIC) undergraduate programme and the graduate International Organization programme are open to all countries.

Undergraduate call (2027 intake, embassy track): the 2027 table invites 74 countries: Afghanistan, Angola, Azerbaijan, Bahamas, Bangladesh, Bolivia, Brazil, Brunei, Bulgaria, Cambodia, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Czech Republic, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Fiji, Gabon, Ghana, Guatemala, India, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Madagascar, Malaysia, Mexico, Mongolia, Morocco, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, South Sudan, Sri Lanka, Sweden, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Trinidad and Tobago, Turkiye, Turkmenistan, Uganda, Ukraine, Uruguay, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, Vietnam, Yemen and Zimbabwe. The Korean embassy may choose not to recommend a candidate because of local circumstances.

Undergraduate education: a bachelor's applicant must have finished, or be expected to finish, high school or an associate degree; an associate-degree applicant must have finished, or be expected to finish, high school. People who hold a bachelor's degree cannot apply, and people with an associate degree can apply only to a bachelor's programme. Applicants expected to graduate by 31 December 2026 give a certificate of expected graduation first and must send the final certificate and transcript by that date if they pass the first round.

Undergraduate grades: the whole-course grade of the previous programme must meet one of: a score of 80 percent or more, a class rank within the top 20 percent, or a CGPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0. A transcript without a recognised scale needs a conversion document confirmed by the school.

Graduate call (latest published, 2026): the applicant must hold, or be expected to complete by 31 July 2026, a bachelor's degree (for the master's) or a master's degree (for the doctorate). The same grade rule applies (80 percent, top 20 percent, or the CGPA values above) to the most recent degree. Applicants must also meet each university's own extra rules. The 2027 graduate call is not published yet; the Study in Korea page says graduate announcements come in February with applications from February to March.

Health and conduct: all applicants must be in good health, mentally and physically, for the whole programme and have no grounds for disqualification for overseas travel, such as a criminal record.

Excluded: graduates (or expected graduates) of a Korean high school, including international schools, or of a Korean associate degree (undergraduate call) or any Korean university (graduate call); people in their final year at a Korean school or university; people who finished a Korean online curriculum; anyone who earlier received a Korean government scholarship for a degree, including former GKS degree scholars and scholars whose award was cancelled; and people who withdrew from a GKS degree award after selection in recent years (three years in the guidelines). Earlier GKS non-degree exchange or Korean-language-programme scholars may apply. Embassy-track applicants who passed the first round cannot apply again through the university track. Each applicant may apply to one track, one programme, one university and one department.
age_experience_notes: Undergraduate (2027 call): under 25, which means born on or after 1 March 2002. Graduate (latest published, 2026 call): under 40, meaning born after 1 September 1986; academic professors from ODA-recipient countries may be up to under 45 (born after 1 September 1981). No work experience is required for the undergraduate call; for the graduate call a certificate of employment is optional evidence.
funding_summary: NIIED pays up to KRW 5,000,000 of tuition per semester in the undergraduate guideline, the university pays what is above that and the admission fee, an economy airfare for entry into Korea, the Korean-language programme fee of KRW 5,200,000 for the language year, and a monthly allowance. The allowance covers living costs, accommodation, health insurance, Korean-proficiency grants, the TOPIK fee, a settlement allowance and degree-completion grants. In the 2027 undergraduate guideline it is KRW 13,560,000 a year during the language year and KRW 14,400,000 a year during the degree programme. For the latest graduate call it was KRW 14,400,000 a year in the language year and KRW 16,560,000 a year in the degree programme. The period is 5 to 7 years for a bachelor's, 3 to 4 years for an associate degree, 3 years for a master's and 4 years for a doctorate, each including one language year unless exempt.
programmes_note: All academic fields set up by the participating universities may be chosen, but only the universities and departments on the 'University Information' file attached to the GKS notice can be applied to. Evening, short-term, online and distance programmes do not count. After final selection a change of field is not allowed. Undergraduate applicants to science and engineering departments get 5 percent extra points. The graduate track also has R&D (science and engineering, with 60 departments in 25 institutions in the 2026 call) and Global Network (humanities and social sciences, master's only, seven departments in six institutions) programmes selected by the universities. The undergraduate UIC programme offers the departments listed below.
institutions_note: Undergraduate embassy track, Type A (28 universities): Ajou, Chung-Ang, Dongguk, Ewha Womans, Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, Hansung, Hanyang, Hongik, Incheon National, Inha, Kookmin, Korea, Kyungdong, Kyung Hee, Myongji, POSTECH, Sejong, Seokyeong, Seoul National, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Sogang, Soongsil, Sungkyunkwan, Sungshin Women's, The Catholic University of Korea, UNIST, University of Seoul and Yonsei. Type B regional universities number 42 in the same call (for example Busan University of Foreign Studies, Chonnam National, Chungnam National, Kyungpook National, Pusan National, Jeju National and Yeungnam). General and Overseas Korean applicants choose up to three different universities in any order and at least one must be Type B; R-GKS applicants choose up to two Type B universities. University track applicants name one university and one department. The latest graduate call listed 35 Type A and 41 Type B institutions, and graduate embassy applicants also choose up to three universities including at least one Type B. Study in Korea says GKS includes over 80 universities in all. Embassy-track applicants should spread their choices, because candidates who pass NIIED's round can still fail at the university round if all their universities are very competitive.

summary.detail: Undergraduate track (2027 call): associate degree after 1 year of Korean-language training plus 2 to 3 years of study; bachelor's degree after 1 year of Korean-language training plus 4 to 6 years. Embassy track: General (88 places, 74 countries), Overseas Koreans and Adoptees (7), R-GKS regional universities (61, 52 countries). University track: UIC science and engineering (100 places, 13 institutions, all countries) and Associate Degree (30 places, 9 institutions). Total 286 scholars. Applicants with TOPIK level 5 or 6 skip the language year.

summary.detail: Graduate track (details from the latest published call, 2026; the 2027 call is not out). Master's: 1 year of Korean-language training plus 2 years of degree study. The Global Network programme (humanities and social sciences, master's only, mainly English lectures) skips the language training and lasts up to 2 years. The 2026 call offered 2,000 places: embassy track 800 (General 776, Overseas Koreans and Adoptees 24), university track General 160 and R-GKS 480, Research 5, International Organization 72, R&D 403 and Global Network 80. Applicants need a bachelor's degree, must be under 40, and need a grade of at least 80 percent or a top-20-percent rank.

benefits.limit_text: NIIED pays up to KRW 5,000,000 per semester (undergraduate guideline); the university pays the amount above this and the admission fee
benefits.conditions: Applies to scholars in the degree programme. Not given to research-programme scholars. The graduate guideline says up to KRW 5 million, with no period named.

benefits.limit_text: Korean-language programme fee: KRW 5,200,000 for the language year
benefits.conditions: Not given to scholars exempt from the language year (TOPIK level 5 or 6), to Global Network and Research scholars, or to R&D applicants in fully English-taught programmes.

benefits.limit_text: Undergraduate 2027: KRW 13,560,000 per year (language year), KRW 14,400,000 per year (degree). Graduate 2026: KRW 14,400,000 (language year), KRW 16,560,000 (degree), KRW 20,880,000 (research programme)
benefits.conditions: An all-in subsidy for living costs, accommodation, health insurance, Korean-proficiency grants, TOPIK fee, settlement and degree-completion grants. The amount may change and depends on budget. Scholars exempt from the language year with TOPIK level 5 or 6 get Korean proficiency grants.

benefits.limit_text: Included in the monthly allowance (no separate housing amount)
benefits.conditions: The guidelines name accommodation as one use of the monthly allowance; no separate housing payment is listed.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance is included in the monthly allowance
benefits.conditions: No separate insurance payment is listed. Travel insurance for the trip to Korea is not covered.

benefits.limit_text: Economy-class entry airfare at actual cost
benefits.conditions: Not given to people living in Korea at the final announcement, or entering Korea from a country other than their own. Domestic travel at home and travel insurance for the trip are not covered. In the graduate call the university buys a one-way ticket, and scholars selected in China and the Czech Republic get no airfare under agreements with those governments.

requirements.text: Form 1 Application Form (in English), Form 2 Personal Statement and Form 3 Study Plan (English or Korean). Embassy track: filled in directly in the online system, then printed with an original handwritten signature after the first round. University track: as instructed by the university.

One recommendation letter (Form 4 in the undergraduate call, Form 5 in the graduate call), signed by a credible person who can judge the applicant's academic ability (a school principal or teacher; for graduates a supervising professor, department head or specialist). It must be dated within one year of the application deadline, and the original is submitted after the first round.
GKS Applicant Agreement and Consent to Collect and Use Personal Information, completed and signed.
Personal Medical Assessment form, completed, with the original sent after the first round.

Proof of citizenship of the applicant and both parents, and proof of the family relationship: an official birth certificate or family register. If a parent is absent (divorced or deceased), extra documents explain this. If citizenship is not shown, passport copies are added. Ethnic group, birthplace or residence do not count as proof of citizenship.

High school graduation certificate (or certificate of expected graduation) and, if applicable, associate degree certificate for undergraduate applicants; bachelor's (and for doctoral applicants, master's) graduation certificate or diploma for graduate applicants. The final paper must show the graduation date and be apostilled or consular confirmed with a certified translation if it is not in English or Korean.

Official academic transcript of the previous programme showing the CGPA or class rank. A converted transcript confirmed by the school is needed if the scale is not 4.0, 4.3, 4.5, 5.0 or 100 points. Apostille or consular confirmation is required for the second round.
TOPIK score report (original) or TOEFL iBT/IELTS score report (copy). Optional, but it earns language points, and TOPIK level 5 or 6 gives an exemption from the language year.

Copy of the applicant's passport (required in the undergraduate call; in the graduate call a supplementary document if the proof of citizenship does not show citizenship). The English name on the application must match the passport.
Proof of Overseas Korean or adoptee status, proof of Korean citizenship renunciation, and proof of descent from a Korean War veteran of a foreign army.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants in those situations

requirements.text: Awards and other certificates: up to 5 documents on activities or achievements from high school onward (undergraduate call), no apostille needed.
Form 4 Research Proposal and a Letter of Invitation from the research programme university.

application_steps.title: Check your country is invited and pick a track
application_steps.detail: The embassy track (General, Overseas Koreans and Adoptees, R-GKS) is open only to citizens of invited countries and goes through the Korean embassy in your country. The university track (UIC, associate degree, and for graduates General, R-GKS, Research, International Organization, R&D and Global Network) goes directly to a university. You may use only one track and one programme. The undergraduate embassy-track application window ran from 15 to 30 September 2026; the university track runs September to November 2026 on each university's own schedule.

application_steps.title: Choose universities and departments from the official list
application_steps.detail: Pick only universities and departments from the University Information file attached to the GKS notice. Embassy-track General applicants choose up to three universities, at least one regional (Type B); R-GKS applicants choose up to two Type B universities. Do not apply to several departments at one university. Check each university's extra language or major rules.

application_steps.title: Submit the application online or to the university
application_steps.detail: Embassy track: register on the Study in Korea website, fill in the forms online and upload scanned certificates. University track: send the forms and certificates as the university instructs (in person or by post). Check the name matches your passport and that nothing is missing, because missing documents or signatures can remove the application.

application_steps.title: First round by the embassy or university
application_steps.detail: The embassy (embassy track) or university (university track) reviews the application. Embassy first-round results came by 16 October 2026 in the undergraduate call. Applicants who pass send the printed signed forms and apostilled or consular-confirmed certificates, with copies of translations where needed, to the embassy or university for NIIED. Embassy-track applicants who fail may still apply to the university track.

application_steps.title: Second round by NIIED and third round by universities
application_steps.detail: NIIED checks eligibility (citizenship, education, grades) and then competency: academic performance, language, activities, contribution to society and international exchange, potential, and the completeness and authenticity of documents. Extra points go to TOPIK level 3 or above, to descendants of Korean War veterans and to science and engineering applicants; overseas Koreans and applicants from low-income backgrounds are preferred. In the graduate call there is no oral interview at NIIED. Embassy-track candidates who pass NIIED are then reviewed by the universities they chose; the university track has no third round.

application_steps.title: Final announcement by NIIED
application_steps.detail: NIIED posts the final scholars on the Study in Korea site; the 2027 undergraduate result is expected on 7 January 2027. NIIED does not inform applicants one by one, so applicants must check the site and their My Page. Embassy-track scholars choose their final university in the Study in Korea system by 29 December 2026 in the undergraduate call. The reasons for passing or failing are not given.

application_steps.title: Receive the invitation, start language training and get a visa
application_steps.detail: Invitation letters and entry guidance are sent to the personal email within January 2027 in the undergraduate call. Scholars with TOPIK level 5 or 6 go straight to the degree programme; all others take the Korean-language year first. Scholars should prepare several apostilled or consular-confirmed copies of their graduation certificate for the university, the embassy (visa) and the immigration office. If the visa is not issued in the entry period, the award may be cancelled.

application_steps.title: Keep to the scholarship rules
application_steps.detail: A change of field after final selection is not allowed. Withdrawal needs a signed renunciation letter sent through the embassy or university to NIIED; it cannot be reversed and the person cannot apply again. A scholar who withdraws within the first 3 months after enrolling must repay everything received since selection. Scholars must follow Korean immigration law and the academic rules of NIIED and the university.

fetch_problems: The Korean embassy's download of the 2026 GKS-G guideline zip file did not complete; the same NIIED document was read as a PDF hosted by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The University Information files (lists of departments and their rules) are attached to the notice pages as zip or spreadsheet files and were not read, so full department lists are not included.
notes: The 2027 undergraduate embassy-track window (15 to 30 September 2026) has already closed as of 13 November 2026. The university track runs to November 2026, and applicants who failed the embassy first round may still apply to it.
Stored data said the graduate applicant age is under 40 and the GPA 80 percent; both are re-confirmed from the 2026 graduate call but not yet from a 2027 graduate call.

Stored benefit 'living allowance KRW 14,400,000 per year during the degree programme' matches the 2027 undergraduate guideline; for graduates the 2026 call gives KRW 16,560,000 in the degree programme and KRW 14,400,000 in the language year.

The Study in Korea page says about 280 undergraduate and 1,600 graduate places in one place and 286 and 2,000 in its tables; the guidelines say 286 for the 2027 undergraduate call and 2,000 for the 2026 graduate call.
UIC department rows were taken from a table whose layout makes the link between a department and its university somewhat uncertain; check them against the guideline before display.

The GKS also has a Research programme (6 months or 1 year, tuition and language fees not given) and Korea-Japan and exchange-student programmes; they are outside the stored degree levels and are not described here.
